subject: BrightCart fanout compression triage and roadmap gating questions
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Lena Wu <lena.wu@brightcart.com>, BrightCart SRE <sre@brightcart.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: BrightCart fanout compression triage and roadmap gating questions

Team —

Over the last ~90 minutes BrightCart (prod region us-west-2) has experienced a ~35% drop in overall QPS for Gen endpoint /v1/generate, concurrent with a 12–18% increase in p50 and a 40% increase in p95 for a subset of multi-turn flows. We see the following signals:

- Request rate from BrightCart's prod key down 33% vs rolling baseline (alerts from usage-synth).
- Per-host kernel sched logs show spikes in throttling events between 07:40–08:20 PST (attached snippet SUP-4293-log-snippet.txt).
- Prefix/KV cache miss rate for model crimson-7b-qat rose from 2% -> 26% (metrics snapshot attached).

Immediate asks:
1) SRE (Ben/Soojin): Can you run the protective traffic-shape (route 10% of BrightCart to crimson-7b-quant-alt) and temporarily lift the concurrency cap on their dedicated pool? If we can restore effective QPS within 30–60m that will buy time. Please open a JIRA and reference SUP-4293.
2) Eng (Karthik): Quick check on recent kernel selector/quant patches — is there a safe rollback command we can flip without a full deploy? Suspect a kernel scheduling regression interacting with quant warmstart.
3) Product (Priyom): We need a short customer-facing update to send to BrightCart (Lena/Miles) summarizing what we're doing and expected timeline. CS should be prepared to offer a one-week credit if we miss the SLA window.

I've opened SUP-4293 and dropped links to the runbook and live metrics in the related_links field below. Attaching a short metrics snapshot and log snippet.

Naomi
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: metrics_snapshot_20280210.png (png), SUP-4293-log-snippet.txt (text)

Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightCart fanout compression triage and roadmap gating questions

Naomi — looking. A couple quick notes and plan:

- Confirmed the throttling spike on the autoscaler interaction surface; host-level kernel backpressure increased around 07:38 PST.
- Created SUP-4293 (link: https://jira.redwood/sup/SUP-4293) and started an ops bridge.

Immediate actions (in progress):
- Enabling traffic-shape to route 12% of BrightCart traffic to crimson-7b-quant-alt (safe compatibility tested).
- Temporarily bumping concurrency cap by +20% on their dedicated pool (5–10m ops work).
- Forcing a KV cache prewarm on the affected nodes (expecting cache hit improvement in ~10–15m).

If these reduce the p95 we consider this a mitigation path; if not, we will roll the kernel selector flag back. Karthik, please confirm the rollback flag and risk.

Ben
SRE Lead

Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 09:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightCart fanout compression triage and roadmap gating questions

Ben — thanks for the quick ops moves. A few technical details:

- We shipped a kernel-selection tweak in 2028.02.09 [deploy id d-20280209-kselect] that biases the scheduler towards denser packing to reduce GPU utilization for multi-tenant workloads. In isolation this reduces cost by ~6%, but on quantized models the packing causes KV evictions during warmstart windows.
- The rollback is a single runtime flag: runtime.kselector.enable_compact=false. Flipping it reverts to the previous placement heuristics and is non-disruptive (no model reload). We should be able to flip this in the next deploy hop or toggle via feature-flag control-plane.
- Risk: if we immediately flip, we may see a small transient latency bump for other tenants while caches re-warm; mitigated by doing staged toggles per host.

My recommendation:
1) Ben — proceed with the routing + prewarm as planned.
2) If p95 remains > baseline after 30m, set runtime.kselector.enable_compact=false on the affected pool and monitor.

Karthik
Engineering (Runtime)

Subject: Re: BrightCart fanout compression triage and roadmap gating questions

Quick product note on customer comms / roadmap gating:

- For BrightCart I'd propose a two-step customer update: (A) an initial 30–60m "we're mitigating" note that explains the immediate actions and ETA for next update; (B) a follow-up post-mortem within 48–72h that covers root cause and longer-term mitigations.
- Regarding roadmap asks: we should flag the kernel-selection compactness as a hold for customers on quantized model workflows until we have explicit warmstart safety tests in the canary matrix. This means pausing any further compactness rollouts for 2 sprints and adding a warmstart regression test.
- If BrightCart wants an SLA credit, recommend we offer a one-week usage credit tiered at the percentage of downtime — CS can draft the exact language.

Proposed customer facing paragraph below (short):
> Hi Lena — we observed a performance regression impacting a portion of your Gen traffic this morning. Our engineers have applied targeted routing and cache pre-warm to stabilize throughput while we verify a safe rollback of a recent scheduling optimization. We expect normal traffic levels to return within the next 60 minutes; we will provide a post-incident summary in 48–72 hours.

If OK I can get CS to send this; Naomi — want to own the outbound?

PrIyom
Product Manager, Serving

Date: Sun, 12 Feb 2028 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Update: BrightCart Gen endpoint stabilization and next steps

Hi Lena / Miles —

Wanted to follow up with a consolidated update after the actions we took on Friday. Summary:

- What happened: A scheduler placement change we rolled on 2028-02-09 caused elevated KV cache evictions for quantized variants under certain warmstart patterns. This led to a material degradation in effective throughput for a subset of BrightCart flows.
- What we did: Ops routed a portion of traffic to a compatible model variant, forced a targeted KV pre-warm, and Eng toggled the runtime.kselector.enable_compact flag on affected hosts.
- Outcome: Traffic and QPS returned to within 7% of baseline within ~45 minutes after the rollback and prewarm. P95 reduced to baseline; we continued to monitor through the weekend.

Next steps / commitments:
- Short term: We will keep the compact selector disabled for BrightCart's pool until we complete warmstart regression tests (target: 2 sprints).
- Post-mortem: Delivery within 48–72 hours with timeline, root cause, and longer-term mitigation (canary/warmstart tests + rollout guardrails).
- Compensation: If you confirm SLA impact on your side, we will coordinate CS to issue a usage credit; happy to discuss details.

Apologies for the disruption — we know reliability is table stakes and appreciate your patience. Would you be available for a 30-minute post-incident call Mon/Tue so we can walk the timeline and proposed mitigations?

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
